drills.q: Implement a trie with insert, search (exact match), and startsWith (prefix match).
drills.a: Each node has children plus an is_end flag; insert walks/creates nodes per character and sets is_end at the last one; search requires the path to exist AND is_end set; startsWith requires only the path to exist.

drills.q: Why is search('ca') different from startsWith('ca') even if only 'car' has been inserted?
drills.a: search must also check is_end at the final node reached; the path to 'ca' exists but is_end is false there, so search returns false while startsWith returns true.

drills.q: Find all dictionary words present in a character grid (Word Search II).
drills.a: Build a trie from the dictionary, then run one DFS from every grid cell following the trie in parallel with the grid path, pruning the moment the current path isn't any word's prefix (trie-child miss).

drills.q: Support search queries with a '.' wildcard matching any single character, backed by a trie.
drills.a: At a normal character follow the matching child; at '.', recursively try every existing child and succeed if any branch matches. Worst case O(26^k * L) for k wildcards.

drills.q: Given a dictionary of roots and a sentence, replace each word with its shortest matching root if one exists.
drills.a: Build a trie from the roots; for each sentence word, walk the trie and stop at the FIRST is_end node encountered (not the longest path) — that's the shortest valid root.

drills.q: Design an autocomplete system that ranks suggestions by query frequency rather than lexicographic order, without recomputing top-k on every keystroke.
drills.a: Maintain a cached top-k list at (or reachable from) each trie node representing a complete query, updated incrementally on writes, rather than DFS-ing the whole subtree per keystroke — full-subtree DFS on a popular short prefix is effectively O(n).
